rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a usable blastocyst and acknowledges limits of a single still image, but it softens or partially misstates the provided lab grade by calling TE moderate/B despite the assigned 3AB having A-grade ICM and B-grade TE, and some image-specific features are described somewhat generically.
Thoroughly integrates maternal age, ovarian reserve, endometriosis, semen parameters, BMI, prior cycle history, and especially thin endometrium into prognosis and transfer context.

Reasoning is logical and well structured, with prognosis tied to embryo quality and uterine factors; minor issue is some ambiguity around exact morphology versus the assigned grade and a few speculative modifiers.

Generally aligned with Gardner grading concepts and evidence-based IVF practice, including caution about thin lining and avoiding unsupported add-ons; slight overemphasis on endometrial thickness as the dominant determinant and some speculative discussion lower it from perfect.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer, counseling, luteal support review, consideration of fresh versus freeze-all, uterine evaluation if failure occurs, and when to consider PGT-A or male-factor follow-up.
